title: Nightmare Inspector: Yumekui Kenbun
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In 1920s Tokyo, Hiruko, a dream-eating baku in the form of a boy, takes clients at the Ginseikan tea house into their nightmares in exchange for the taste of them. Episodic stories of grief, failure and hidden cruelty gradually build a continuing plot about Hiruko's origin, a rival shop that feeds clients fantasies, and the tea-house owner Mizuki.
life_message: Facing the truth of one's own grief and guilt, however painful, rather than hiding in illusion.

content.note: Mutilation, a dream massacre and grotesque imagery (ANN column; MU Child Abuse, Tragedy).
Nightmare horror, described as 'sometimes sicker than you'd expect' (ANN column; AniList Horror).
Suggestive scenes between pretty boys and fan-service omake chapters; nothing explicit (ANN column).
Repressed memories, hallucinations, grief and child abuse in clients' stories (MU categories; ANN column).

folkways.japan: Draws on the baku of Japanese folklore and Taisho-era decadence, describing a society where respectable surfaces hide private shame.
